subject: Short-term triage access authorization request - LUM-3892
messages:
From: Nora Patel <nora.patel@luminexa.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: short access window to logs for triage (LUM-3892)

Hi Irene,

We hit an intermittent inference regression in production for one customer stream (LUM-3892) and our engineers need a short, timeboxed access window to pull recent request/response logs and the associated KV cache snapshots to complete triage. We typically keep logs for 7 days but the particular traces we need were purged under the current retention and we don’t have a local copy.

Can Redwood enable a 48-hour exception so we can export the relevant traces (filtered to tenant:luminexa and request IDs: 8f7a, 8f7b, 8f9c)? We will only pull the minimum fields needed for debugging (timestamps, request/response, model/variant, non-sensitive metadata). We will not request full customer prompt text unless absolutely necessary and will redact if asked.

Attached is a short incident summary and the ticket link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/LUM-3892. We need the window to begin as soon as possible; acceptance criteria: export delivered and logs deleted from the temporary storage after confirmation.

Thanks — appreciate any fast help here.

— Nora
Nora Patel
Sr. SRE, Luminexa
Attachments: luminexa_incident_summary.pdf (1 page)
From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: Nora Patel <nora.patel@luminexa.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 09:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short access window to logs for triage (LUM-3892)

Nora —

Thanks for the clear summary and the ticket link. I’m looping in Marcus (ops) and Priyom (security/compliance) to approve and coordinate the access. A couple of follow-ups from our side before we proceed:

- Scope: confirm the exact time range and the minimal list of request IDs you will pull.
- Fields: confirm you only need metadata + token-level outputs if required; say explicitly if you need unredacted prompt text.
- Delivery: how do you want the export delivered? Encrypted S3 with a one-time download link or a secure SFTP?
- Post-work: we require an audit log entry and confirmation that the temporary copy is destroyed within the approved window.

Marcus/Priyom — can we approve a short access window for this triage? Nora is requesting 48 hours; I would prefer we limit to the minimum viable time and record the exception. I’ve attached the incident summary they sent.

Irene Choi
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Nora Patel <nora.patel@luminexa.com>, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short access window to logs for triage (LUM-3892)

Thanks for flagging, Nora.

Irene — I’m comfortable green-lighting a timeboxed exception for triage with constraints:
- Approve a 36-hour export window (start when we enable access), not 48.
- Export must be scoped to tenant:luminexa + the three request IDs listed (8f7a, 8f7b, 8f9c) and the narrowest timestamp range possible.
- Delivery via encrypted S3 with one-time presigned URL (24h expiry).
- Redwood will create an audit record and a snapshot ID; export must be removed and documented once confirmed by Luminexa.

Priyom — please give compliance sign-off on the redaction rules (any PII removed) and confirm the exception form. If you OK, Irene please proceed with the technical steps and notify us when the presigned URL is ready.

Marcus Lin
Director, Inference Ops
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Nora Patel <nora.patel@luminexa.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short access window to logs for triage (LUM-3892)

Nora/Team —

Compliance sign-off granted with conditions:
1) Timebox: 36 hours maximum. Start timestamp must be recorded in the audit entry at enablement.
2) Scope: only the three request IDs and the narrowest timestamp window for those traces. No broad tenant-wide export.
3) Redaction: remove or mask any end-user PII (emails, phone numbers, payment identifiers). If raw prompt text is required, Luminexa must clearly justify it in the exception form.
4) Audit & retention: Redwood will attach an audit record and the export SHA256 fingerprint to the exception ticket. Luminexa must acknowledge receipt and confirm deletion within the window.
5) Delivery: encrypted S3 presigned URL (24h expiry) only. No long-term storage on Redwood.

I’ve attached the signed exception form and an internal checklist for the operator: access_exception_form.docx. Please complete the form fields for justification and sign the DocuSign link before we enable the export. Once completed, Irene please coordinate with Ops to create the export and post the presigned link to the ticket.

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/some-signature-link/ABC123
Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/LUM-3892

If Luminexa cannot accept redaction, we will need explicit legal review which adds time — let us know.

Thanks — Priyom
Priyom Das
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
Attachments: access_exception_form.docx (fillable), internal_export_checklist.md (operator steps)
